description: Extend the project AI-quality surface with a per-bucket first-time-right + rework series and render it as a Dashboard FTR trend line with an optional rework overlay.

tasks.title: Expose per-bucket FTR + rework trend series on the AI-quality surface
tasks.description: Extend `IssueQuerier.GetQualityAsync` to produce a pre-sized 30-day daily `Trend` series (per-bucket FTR rate + per-bucket rework-at-any-stage rate) in the same single pass that already computes the 7d/30d scalars — reusing `ClassifyRuns` verbatim with no second quality path. Add `QualityTrendDto` / `QualityTrendPointDto` to `IssueRoutes.Dtos.cs` and map the additive `Trend` field in `IssueRoutes.QualityMetrics.cs`'s `BuildResponse`, leaving the existing windows unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: `GET /api/projects/{ref}/issues/metrics/quality` returns an additive `trend` object whose `Points` is a pre-sized 30-element daily array spanning `Window30d.From`..`To`, with `Bucket: "day"`.

Each `QualityTrendPointDto` exposes `Boundary` (yyyy-MM-dd), `SampleCount`, nullable `FirstTimeRightRate`, nullable `ReworkRate`; both rates are null iff `SampleCount == 0` (empty bucket independent of siblings, never 0%/100%).
Per-bucket FTR rate = first-time-right shipped-in-bucket / all shipped-in-bucket, reusing the existing first-time-right classification (no new event/state/write).

Per-bucket rework rate = reworked-at-any-stage / all shipped-in-bucket, where any-stage is `stageRework.Values.Any(v => v)` over the existing per-stage classification; an issue reworked at multiple stages counts exactly once.
Bucket membership is anchored on ship time (`com.mohist.issue.work-completed`, latest wins); issues that never reached `Done` contribute to no bucket.
The existing `Window7d`/`Window30d` single-point contract and zero-sample empty result are unchanged in shape and semantics; a zero-sample project returns `200` with null per-bucket rates.
An unknown project reference returns `404`, consistent with the existing endpoint.

`IssueQuerierSpecs` cover per-bucket FTR rate, per-bucket rework-any-stage rate, multi-stage-counts-once, empty-bucket-null-independent, non-shipped-excluded, ship-time anchoring, and additive-unchanged-scalars.
`IssueMetricsApiSpecs` cover trend alongside windows, zero-sample `200` with null per-bucket rates, and `404`.
`npm test` (server) passes with no warnings (TreatWarningsAsErrors).
tasks.output: packages/server: extended `IssueQuerier.GetQualityAsync` + `QualityTrendDto`/`QualityTrendPointDto` in `IssueRoutes.Dtos.cs` + `Trend` mapping in `IssueRoutes.QualityMetrics.cs`, with passing `IssueQuerierSpecs` and `IssueMetricsApiSpecs`.
tasks.notes: Mirror the pre-sized daily boundary idiom from `GetCompletionBucketsAsync` (IssueQuerier.cs:345) and `BuildWindow`'s nullability rule (IssueQuerier.cs:720-722). The trend is fed from the same single `ClassifyRuns` pass as the scalars — add only an in-memory `QualityTrendAccumulator[30]` indexed by ship-day boundary (design D4). `now` stays an injected `DateTimeOffset`.

tasks.title: Render the FTR trend line widget with optional rework overlay in the Productivity zone
tasks.description: Build `pages/dashboard/productivity/FtrTrendChart.tsx` consuming the additive `trend` field from the existing `useQualityMetrics()` hook (one fetch), composed against the chart baseline (`ChartContainer`/`ChartAccessibility`/`LineSeries`/`ChartAxes`/`ChartLegend`). Render one FTR point per daily bucket on a single 0–100% axis, with an optional rework-rate overlay toggled by local state; gap the line at null buckets. Mount it in `ProductivityZone.tsx` right after `QualityPanel`.
acceptanceCriteria: `FtrTrendChart` is mounted in `ProductivityZone.tsx` immediately after `QualityPanel`; the existing 7d/30d `QualityPanel` scalars remain untouched.
The widget calls the existing `useQualityMetrics()` hook once (no second fetch); a missing/undefined `trend` field renders the empty state (graceful degradation against an older server).
Loading, error, and empty states route through `ChartContainer`; the empty state names the concrete next action (the line gains data once an issue ships within the trailing window).

In the resolved state the FTR `LineSeries` renders one point per bucket whose value is the per-bucket FTR rate sourced from the series; a bucket with a null FTR rate produces a `null` entry that gaps the line (no 0%/100% plotted).
The rework overlay renders on the same 0–100% axis, is toggleable via local `useState`, and sources its per-bucket rate from the series (never derived client-side from the FTR line).
The legend disambiguates the FTR series from the rework series by shape (e.g. solid vs dashed swatch) so a color-blind user can tell them apart; `ChartAccessibility` provides an SR summary.
All colors come from `--chart-*` tokens; numeric labels use `tabular-nums`; motion is transform-based and `prefers-reduced-motion`-aware.
The widget is read-only: it performs no write/mutation against issue, session, or workflow state.
`FtrTrendChart.test.tsx` covers loading/error/empty/resolved states, trend values sourced from the series, overlay toggle, null-bucket no-point, legend shape disambiguation, and the SR summary.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass.
tasks.output: packages/web: optional `trend` field in `entities/issue/api/quality-metrics.ts`, new `pages/dashboard/productivity/FtrTrendChart.tsx` + `.test.tsx`, mounted in `ProductivityZone.tsx`.
tasks.notes: Compose strictly against the existing `pages/dashboard/charts/` baseline from prerequisite 294 — introduce no new chart library or primitive (design D5/D6). Reuse `LineSeries`'s `(LinePoint | null)[]` segment-splitting for null-bucket gaps (LineSeries.tsx:15). The DTO `trend` field must be optional (`trend?`) so an old server omitting it leaves the widget in the empty state.
